side_white_day.title: White Day
side_white_day.beats:
March 14, White Day: a month after Valentine's, whoever received chocolate returns the favor, ideally with something sweeter and, by a rule nobody can trace, worth three times as much. The school year is nearly over, the third-years' graduation is close and spring break hangs over both Hero Course classes.

Default course as pressure: Tenya Iida has a spreadsheet of who gave what, what a triple return would cost and a bow rehearsed for each name. Shoto Todoroki takes the three-times rule literally and returns three of everything. Katsuki Bakugo, who cooks better than he admits, leaves a tray of perfect homemade cookies on the lounge table with a note reading "Don't make it weird" and is gone before anyone can thank him. Rikido Sato bakes for everyone who came to his February workshop. Minoru Mineta returns his class-wide chocolate with a long, formal speech. Denki Kaminari forgot entirely and sprints to the Campus Store at lunch. Eijiro Kirishima hands out his returns with a fist bump each. In Class 1-B, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu tears up over a card of thanks, and Neito Monoma gives returns to all of 1-B and, after a long pause, leaves one unsigned box outside 1-A's door.

The heart of the day is thanks that matter: a small return to someone who helped the party through the winter, a classmate who sat by a hospital bed, or a friend who never asked for anything. Friendship first; anything more stays a hint unless the player speaks it.

By path: a Hero Course student gives and receives returns in the dorm and the homerooms; a General Studies student sees Hitoshi Shinso return a February box in person with one awkward, honest line; a Support Course student is offered a free gear upgrade by Mei Hatsume as her version of a return, wanted or not; a Management Course student watches the Campus Store's White Day stock sell out by noon.

The event is complete when the returns are given, the thanks said and the day winds down.
